newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian blue chips seen losing steam.
newsitem.headline: Croatian blue chips seen losing steam.

text.p: Croatian shares closed mixed to higher in livelier trade on Friday, and traders predicted the blue chips could lose steam and some industrial shares could come under the spotlight.

Zagrebacka Banka, which was at the centre of investors' interest in the past three days, closed 10 kuna lower at 1,990. It was the most active issue though, accounting for a half of the day's volume with 7,098 shares.
"The euphoria has come and gone. It lasted but two days," said Marko Nikolac of Metroholding brokerage.
On the news of credit rating and good business results, Zagrebacka's price surged up in London on Wednesday to over $35 per 1/10 GDR, but came down to around $33.6 on Friday.
Nikolac said he could not see it staging any substantial gains in the short term.
Other fully listed shares -- Pliva pharmaceuticals and Varazdinska Banka -- both gained ground on Friday.

Pliva rose five kuna to 470 kuna and Nikolac said it is poised, perhaps, for a similar bull run as Zagrebacka in two weeks time, when it comes out, as expected, with the annual business report, largely thought to be good.

Varazdinska Banka 1-issue gained over 10 percent or 5,000 kuna to 51,000, but on meagre volume of 11 shares. Its 2-issue, also listed in the Zagreb bourse's first quotation, traded 20 kuna up at 1,420, on volume of 117 shares.
"The good thing is that there was some interest in Kras and Elka, and they could do better next week," Nikolac said.
Both companies, chocolate producer Kras and electric cable maker Elka, lost steam after they were put on the list for the mass vaucher privatisation due later this year.
Kras gained 9 kuna to close at 440, trading 390 shares, while Elka inched up 5 kuna to 150, on volume of 50 shares.

Biggest gainer hotelier Riviera gained 19 kuna to 169, trading 210 shares. Of other tourist shares, Jadranturist was not traded at all while Istraturist lost five kuna to 205 and Laguna was steady at 1,470.
Biggest loser, Trgovacka Banka, lost 150 kuna to close at 1,100, selling only 20 shares.
Of 15 active shares eight were up, four down and three remained flat. The turnover was up at 16.8 million, while volume remained at the same level with 11,931 shares traded.
